newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hopeful Pyongyang to join formal peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hopeful Pyongyang to join formal peace talks.

text.p: The United States, after a day-long meeting on Wednesday with North and South Korea, said it was hopeful the isolationist North would join international talks on a peace treaty for the Korean peninsula.

Following the first occasion that diplomats from the bitter Korean rivals had sat down together at the same table to discuss peace, the head of the North Korean delegation said the approximately four hours of discussions took place "in a sincere atmosphere".

In Washington, U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters that "there were no breakthroughs but the United States is hopeful that today's talks will lead to North Koera joining the formal four-party talks."

Last April, President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam proposed to the Stalinist North Korean government that four-way talks including China, take place to forge a new agreement to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

"Other than the fact that they came to a joint briefing, which is itself a rather positive response to our proposal ... I believe the joint briefing itself is modest progress," a senior State Department official said after the gathering in Manhattan's plush Hilton Hotel.
"North Korean diplomats have sat down with South Korean and American diplomats to talk about the possibility of getting to peace talks and that beats all of the alternatives."
The North Korean delegation now plans to report to Pyongyang on the discussions, but there was no indication when they might reply to the proposals, U.S. officials said.

Wednesday's meeting, described by the U.S. as a "joint briefing," was convened at the request of Pyongyang, which wanted more information on Washington and Seoul's proposals for four-way talks. Actual negotiations may not start until July, according to U.S. officials.

The senior state department official said the U.S. had proposed that the four parties meet, in a place to be decided, at a level to be determined to discuss an agenda for "a peace mechanism and then a peace agreement, no strings attached, everything's on the table."
He said the U.S. was keeping Beijing informed but declined to discuss China's possible role.
South Korean deputy foreign minister Song Young Shik also described Wednesday's meeting in positive terms.

"We consider that this briefing was very significant," Song told reporters. "Although North Korea did not clearly express whether to attend the meeting (peace talks) or not, the fact that North Korea listened attentively to the briefing ... and studied the proposal, it can be assessed as positive."

The gathering took place during a tense period in the peninsula, including a string of defections from the North and reports of famine and economic collapse in the Stalinist state long allied with China and the former Soviet Union.

North Korea has twice delayed taking part in the briefing in what was seen as an effort to press Washington to provide more food aid. Pyongyang had been demanding that the armistice be scrapped to pave the way for a peace treaty, but solely with Washington, something unacceptable to Seoul and the United States. U.S. troops fought alongside South Korea during the Korean War, while China supported North Korea.
Witnesses said just before the meeting began the three heads of delegation clasped their hands together, one on top of the other before sitting down at a circular table in a hotel conference room.
An American participant described the meeting as "serious and sincere" and said that North Korean and South Korean officials addressed each other directly.

"It seemed to me that this was in every way the kind of meeting that you would have wanted it to be," he said. "The question of when (the North Korean answer) might occur,, there are really no hints on that but they've got every reason to accept it."

North Korean delegation head Kim Gye Gwan, vice minister for foreign affairs, told reporters through an interpreter: "We are prepared to listen to whatever proposals promote peace and stability on the Korean peninsula. As for the contents of the briefing we heard today, we need further study of these proposals."
Officials from the United States and South Korea were scheduled to meet on Thursday followed by a bilateral meeting between the U.S. and North Korea on Friday.
